subject: FinCo — OpenAI-compatible migration: post-call & test plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@finco.com>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@finco.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: FinCo — OpenAI-compatible migration: post-call & test plan

Hi Sofia / Marcus —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can validate migration risk on your side:

Key takeaways:
- Primary ask: confirm we can swap your existing OpenAI-based calls to Redwood with minimal SDK changes and identical outputs for your core workflows (summarization, customer reply generation, and embeddings).
- Constraints: strict latency targets (p95 <= 400ms for 512-token completions), and token parity for audit pipelines.
- Success criteria: functional parity on a set of 30 golden prompts, streaming parity for live chat, and embeddings cosine similarity >= 0.98 for retrieval-intent queries.

Proposed tests (we attached a formal test plan):
1) Sanity: 10 short prompts (generation/stop tokens) — confirm token counts and stop behavior.
2) Streaming: run 5 concurrent streaming sessions, measure first-byte latency and chunk shapes.
3) Prompt diffs: run your 30 golden prompts and compare outputs (we'll provide a diff tool).
4) Embeddings parity: run 200 queries and compute cosine distribution.
5) Error behavior: exercise rate limit / 429 and 5xx handling to validate client retry logic.

Practical migration guidance (short):
- API surface: Redwood supports an OpenAI-compatible REST surface (same paths for chat/completions/embeddings) but we recommend swapping to the Redwood SDK to get connection pooling and our model-mapping helpers. Example curl is in the attached test plan.
- SDK swap: in most services a two-line change (client instantiation + api_key) will work; function-calling and JSON-structured responses behave the same but we may have small differences in argument names for advanced features (we document mapping).
- Known diffs: tokenization can differ slightly on edge cases (special whitespace + custom stop sequences). We'll log these in the prompt diffs artifact.

Next steps I propose:
- You run the attached test plan (FinCo test plan.xlsx) against a Redwood dev endpoint we’ll provision.
- We schedule a 60-min joint debug session next week to review the prompt diffs and streaming traces.

Deliverables I will send today:
- A migration test workspace (API key + endpoint)
- The result-diff script (example-prompt-diffs.txt)
- A matrix comparing Redwood vs major hyperscalers for performance/cost (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.pdf)

If that looks good I’ll provision the workspace and send the invite for the test session.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0211

Attachments: finco-migration-test-plan.xlsx, example-prompt-diffs.txt, redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.pdf

From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@finco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@finco.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinCo — OpenAI-compatible migration: post-call & test plan

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and clear plan. A couple of clarifying questions before we start the tests: 

1) For streaming parity — our front-end relies on chunked partial outputs that include role metadata and delta tokens. Do you replicate the same chunk envelope (role/content/delta) exactly or is there any restructuring in Redwood’s stream?

2) On embeddings: which model would you map to our current openai-embedding-002 calls? We need to ensure our vector index remains stable (rebuild is costly).

3) Cost estimate: can you give a ballpark per-1M-token comparison vs the hyperscalers for our expected monthly volume (~50M tokens)? The matrix was useful but wanted to see numbers with our expected mix.

We’ll run the tests next Monday — Marcus will own the run and I’ll join the debug session. If you can provision the workspace and API key by EOD Friday that’d be great.

Sofia Ramos
Sr. AI Platform Engineer, FinCo
sofia.ramos@finco.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: FW: FinCo — OpenAI-compatible migration: post-call & test plan

Marissa / Dev —

Copying our internal notes and immediate action items before I reply to Sofia with technical details: 

Action items (internal):
- Dev: provision the FinCo dev workspace (dev key, endpoint in us-west) and enable stream logs for 72 hours. Please also enable the "openai_compat" header mode so we can surface any mapping differences in responses.
- Me: prepare mapping doc for embeddings (recommend mapping: redwood-embed-002 -> nearest parity to openai-embedding-002; include vector normalization notes).
- Marissa: provide Sofia the approximate cost calc for 50M tokens using our typical mix (70% generation, 30% embeddings). I'll add margin for batching efficiency.

Technical notes to include in reply to FinCo:
- Streaming envelope: Redwood’s stream uses the same delta chunks for chat but includes an extra `x-chunk-id` header for traceability. The JSON envelope body preserves role/delta fields so front-end parsing should be identical.
- Tokenization: differences are <1% on our internal corpus; we’ll include token-by-token diffs for problematic prompts.
- Embedding parity: recommend running an initial small sample (200 vectors) against both endpoints and compute cosine mean/std; if below threshold we can run a controlled reindex procedure with dependencies.

Snippet for FinCo to run (OpenAI-compatible curl):

curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood-internal.test/v1/chat/completions" 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_DEV_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.1-openai-compat","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the following ticket"}],"stream":true}'

And Python SDK quick swap example (drop-in):

# pip install redwood-sdk
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_DEV_KEY")
resp = client.chat.create(model="redwood-1.1-openai-compat", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the ticket"}], stream=True)

I’ll finish the mapping doc and the example diff script and then reply to Sofia directly.

-Camila
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@finco.com>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@finco.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Jul 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinCo — OpenAI-compatible migration: post-call & test plan

Thanks Sofia — quick answers and next steps: 

1) Streaming: as Camila noted, chunk envelope is preserved. The only difference is an additional header (`x-chunk-id`) which is safe to ignore on your client; role/delta pieces are unchanged so your front-end should work without change. We’ll include a small sample stream trace in the workspace.

2) Embedding mapping: our recommendation is `redwood-embed-002` for parity with `openai-embedding-002`. We expect mean cosine >= 0.985 on typical retrieval queries; if you observe drift we can run a partial reindex controlled by metadata to limit cost.

3) Cost estimate (ballpark for 50M monthly tokens):
- Hyperscaler A (your current provider): ~$1,800 USD per 1M tokens generation-equivalent -> approx $90,000/month
- Redwood (projected with batching and KV-cache benefits): ~$1,200 USD per 1M tokens -> approx $60,000/month
- Note: embeddings priced separately; estimated embeddings spend ~ $6,000/month depending on vector size and ops.

We’ll provision the dev workspace by EOD Friday (Dev is on it) and attach the API key + the sample results. Plan for the test run on Monday; we’ll join the debug call Tuesday 09:30 PT to review diffs.

If Marcus or Sofia want any additional prompts included in the golden set please send them by EOD Sunday.

Thanks — looking forward to the test run.

Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: finco-migration-test-plan.xlsx, redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.pdf
